title: Hero button contrast on gradient backgrounds

patterns: theme-switched hero without companion button override

rule.summary: When theming a hero section with gradient backgrounds, each theme MUST provide an explicit `.hero .btn` override — inheriting `--clr-accent` from the base style sheet produces invisible buttons on dark gradients.
rule.details: The base `styles.css` hero btn uses `background: var(--clr-primary)` with `color: var(--clr-white)` — safe because `--clr-primary` is always dark. But theme variants like Azul and Oscuro redefine `--clr-accent` as a bright blue (#3182ce, #38bdf8). If the hero btn references `--clr-accent` instead of `--clr-primary`, the button merges into the gradient. Fix: each theme CSS must include `.hero .btn { background: <solid-readable> }`.
rule.check: For each theme, assert `window.getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.hero .btn')).backgroundColor` !== `'rgba(0,0,0,0)'` and contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 against both the hero background and the button text.
rule.fix: `.hero .btn { background: var(--clr-primary); color: var(--clr-white); }` — use a color that contrasts against BOTH the background gradient AND the text color.

evidence.description: Azul/Oscuro themes: changed hero btn from `var(--clr-accent)` to `var(--clr-primary)`
44/44 checks pass after fix — Playwright rendered audit across 4 themes
evidence.method: Playwright page.evaluate per theme, contrast ratio math
